en.explorer.dirMissing: Directory does not exist or was deleted
en.explorer.localSession:
This session is a local workspace and does not use remote files.

To access remote, set a machine as "current" in Settings, then pick a remote workspace with the "…" button above.
en.explorer.notConnected: Not connected to the remote host (after a restart, set a machine as "current" in Settings, or refresh the right column)
en.explorer.sessionLocal: This session does not use a remote workspace
en.file.binary: Binary file ({size}) — use "Download", rw_download or the local mirror to view.
en.file.conflict: The remote file changed, please re-read it
en.file.linkUnresolved: This file link does not map onto a remote path (the Session workspace is not a remote mirror directory). Open it from the sidebar "Remote Files" tab, or read it with rw_read_file.
en.file.truncated: … content truncated (read-only remote view; use rw_read_file / Download for the full file)
en.picker.hintKeys: Enter confirms · Esc closes · Ctrl/⌘+Enter sets workspace
en.picker.localIntro: Opens the system folder dialog; when unavailable, uses the built-in directory browser. You can also type a local path directly.
en.picker.noHomeWin: Windows remotes do not support ~ resolution — enter an absolute path
en.picker.noMachines: No machines yet — add one in Settings first
en.picker.noSubdir: (no subdirectories — you can use the current directory)
en.picker.noSysPicker: Cannot open the system folder picker — you can type a local path in the input box
en.picker.noSysPickerHost: This system cannot auto-open a directory picker — type a local path in the input box
en.picker.timeout: Directory selection timed out — retry or type a local path directly
en.picker.title: Select working directory
en.picker.typePath: — type a local path in the input box instead
en.settings.added: Added — you can set it as current
en.settings.advExpand: ▼ Advanced (private key / proxy jump / agent, etc.)
en.settings.auditEmpty: No records yet (commands run remotely are logged to $DSH_HOME/remote-workspaces/audit.log)
en.settings.backendNative: native (built-in ssh2: password / key / agent / OTP)
en.settings.backendOpensshAliasOk: "Use a ~/.ssh/config alias" is on: the name is handed to ssh verbatim, and Port/User/IdentityFile/ProxyJump come from that Host block — the matching fields below have no effect (this is the "one source of truth" case, issue #50). A password/passphrase is still offered to ssh through askpass, and is only used if the Host block has no usable authentication.
en.settings.backendOpensshHint: Delegates the transport to the local `ssh`, so the whole of ~/.ssh/config applies: GSSAPI/Kerberos (log in once with kinit and no secret is needed), ProxyCommand, PKCS11Provider, Match blocks… Host keys are checked by ssh against your own known_hosts. The cost is a fresh connection per command (slower than native); file browsing over SFTP still reuses one session.
en.settings.cleared: Cleared current remote — local sessions no longer use remote context automatically
en.settings.deployConfirm: Install dsh into a private directory on the remote (no system directory, no PATH change, no replacing the version in use). Continue?
en.settings.deployDone: Deployed; this machine now records the dsh it uses
en.settings.deployHint: A failed connect is usually not the plugin's fault: the remote dsh version or environment is wrong (an old one cannot start the web surface on Linux at all). Check read-only, or install into a private directory on the remote that leaves the user's own version untouched.
en.settings.deployInvestigateStarted: A session was created — follow up there.
en.settings.deployResumed: A deploy is already running — re-attached to its progress
en.settings.filledSsh: Filled from ~/.ssh/config (only references the private key path, never reads its content)
en.settings.intro: Manage multiple SSH machines (password / private key / agent / proxy jump / keychain). Pick a path when creating/selecting a workspace: "Local" opens the system folder dialog; "Remote" picks a machine and a directory on it.
en.settings.name: Name
en.settings.noActive: No active remote machine: saved machines are standby connections and never enter a session context automatically (local sessions are unaffected).
en.settings.noMachines: No machines yet. Add one below.
en.settings.recentWorkspaces: Recent workspaces of the current machine (one-click switch)
en.settings.saveWritesSshConfig: Saving writes host/user/port/key into a managed block in ~/.ssh/config (marked # dsh-remote: managed); the file then takes precedence — edit it directly and it takes effect at once.
en.settings.secretStoreFailed: The OS keychain refused the password ({msg}); it was saved as plaintext in machines.json and the machine still connects.
en.settings.selfUpdateBlocked: ℹ️ This is a link:/dev install (not under node_modules), so self-update is disabled to avoid overwriting source — update it from its source repo.
en.settings.sshAliasHint: Alias mode: the machine remembers only the name "{alias}"; host/user/port/key/jump host are resolved from ~/.ssh/config at every connect, so editing that file takes effect immediately.
en.settings.sshAliasSaved: Saved as an alias (resolved on connect)
en.settings.title: Remote workspace (dsh-remote)
en.settings.updateApplied: ✅ Updated to v{to} ({from} → {to}); the host half hot-swapped in place.
en.settings.updateAppliedNoReload: ✅ Updated to v{to} ({from} → {to}). Restart Harness to apply.
en.settings.updateConfirm: Update dsh-remote to v{version}? This replaces the local plugin files and hot-swaps the host half in place (no Harness restart). Continue?
en.settings.updatePendingReload: ⚠️ v{disk} is on disk but v{loaded} is still running; update again or restart Harness to switch.
en.settings.useSshConfig: Use a ~/.ssh/config alias (keep the alias, not a copy)
en.settings.useSshConfigHint: Fields left empty or at their default (user root, port 22, key, jump host) come from ~/.ssh/config at connect time; a non-default value overrides it.
en.settings.webAttachCmdHint: Set the absolute path when the remote dsh is not on the SSH login PATH (a private prefix, or node installed with nvm), e.g. /home/you/.nvm/versions/node/v22.19.0/bin/node /home/you/.dsh-remote/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js. Empty falls back to the global webAttachCommand.
en.settings.webAttachExisting: Or paste the URL of an interface already running there (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?token=…)
en.settings.webAttachHint: Open the DSH web interface of a remote machine in this browser. The remote never opens an inbound port: this plugin SSHes out, starts a loopback-only dsh web there, and carries its port back over the SSH connection.
en.settings.webAttachTokenWarn: The URL carries a login token. It is for this machine only — do not share it.
